title: Experimentation and Start-up Performance: Evidence from A/B Testing
eligible_reason: Firm-week panel (35,262 startups x 208 weeks, April 5 2015 to March 24 2019) with binary treatment `using_ab_only` (A/B testing tool detected on the firm's website that week) adopted at firm-specific weeks across essentially every week of the panel; 29,118 never-users. Table 2 Model 3 is a static TWFE (week FE + firm FE, no controls, firm-clustered) and is eligible. Complications: 2,732 firms are already using a tool in week 1 (always-treated) and 4,143 of the 6,144 ever-users switch the tool off at least once (Optimizely dropped its free plan in December 2017), so the protocol's switch-off rule (drop post-adoption observations with treatment = 0) must be applied; only 1,241 ever-users are clean single adopters.
design_notes: ab_data.dta: 7,334,496 rows, firm_id (anonymized Crunchbase org), week_id 1-208, balanced panel. using_ab_only = 1 in 8.2% of firm-weeks; ever-treated 6,144 firms, never 29,118; first-treatment week spread over all 208 weeks (2,732 at week 1). Switch patterns among ever-users: (1 on, 1 off) 3,579; (1 on, 0 off) 2,001; (2 on, 1 off) 333; (2 on, 2 off) 202; more complex 29. ab_switcher = 1 for 5,384 firms (within-sample variation). Published Table 2: four models of log1p_pageviews [Log(Visits+1)] on using_ab_only with week FE only (1), firm FE + log1p_stack2 (2), week + firm FE (3), week + firm FE + log1p_stack2 (4); SE clustered by firm_id. Figure 1 spec chart: all variants include log1p_stack2 (time-varying technology-stack control), some add firm-specific linear trends (c.week_id##firm_id) or restrict to switchers or 2x2 week pairs. Figure 2 event study: switchers collapsed to firm-month, eventdd with month FE + firm-specific linear trends + stack control, pooling adopters and dis-adopters (event time reversed for dis-adopters), 18- and 36-month windows. Table 3: generalized synthetic control (R). Figures 4-5 and appendix tables include controls or other datasets. The batch text file is the 2019 NBER working paper (35,918 firms, 173 weeks); the published-version numbers below come from the Harvard DASH author manuscript (Sept 10, 2021), which matches the package (35,262 firms, 208 weeks, 7,334,496 obs).
estimators_reported: event study (eventdd) with unit trends and controls
IV / fuzzy DiD (appendix, Google Optimize 360 launch)

specs.code_line: eststo m3: reghdfe log1p_pageviews using_ab_only, absorb(week_id firm_id) vce(cluster firm_id)

specs.notes: Text: 'accounting for firm-level heterogeneity ... the estimated impact drops to 55%'. For CSA/BJS: treat first adoption week as cohort, drop firm-weeks after adoption with using_ab_only = 0 (switch-off rule), always-treated (week-1 users) contribute no identifying variation.

screener_notes: Package: ~/did_packages/mnsc/mnsc.2021.4209/replication_package_MS-ENI-19-02875/ with README.txt, ab_data.dta (main firm-week panel), ab_product_metrics.dta, ab_wayback.dta, google_360_data.dta / .csv, analysis_of_ab_data_public.do (all Stata tables/figures), analysis_synthetic_controls_public.R (Table 3, Figures 3 and A5). Source data (Crunchbase, BuiltWith, SimilarWeb) are licensed; firm identifiers anonymized; cleaning code not shared. The one eligible spec is Table 2 col 3 (0.553, SE 0.026). Re-estimation must handle (a) 2,732 always-treated firms, (b) extensive switch-off (4,143 of 6,144 ever-users), (c) first-adoption cohorts in nearly every one of 208 weeks (consider monthly aggregation of cohorts only as a sensitivity, not for the headline replication). Note the data in the batch text (NBER WP 2019: 35,918 firms, 173 weeks, Table 3 col 2 0.464) differ from the published version; the package matches the published version.
